finding: FUZZ-M10-24H-A, the rebase-orphan shape (the final-tree 24 h run at 4f4849e, 2026-10-04; curve seed 20277239, minimised from 274 actions; harness, not program): the wind-down's second claim pass required `lender_sol` at most the hooks' dust cap (0.01 SOL) and failed with nothing owed to any lender and 42,774,727 lamports in `lender_sol` (53,917,548 in the full run). Settlements had shrunk the pool's token claims until the share epoch rolled with a rebase, which floors each lender's shares and `S` separately and so leaves up to one share per lender in `S` that no lender holds (ECON §9.5); the lenders then withdrew while a vest ran — a lender is paid the unreleased vest only when its burn takes `S` to 0 (R3B-2), which the orphan shares prevent — so the pass's crank released the vest to the orphan shares, whose SOL is claimable by nobody (ECON §9.4 I-P6: the wind-down's residue is rounding plus rebase-orphan credits; the hooks' `invariants::lender::liveness` accepts it when no entitlement is unpaid). Here every lender had left, so the 2 orphan shares were all of `S`. The orphan credit failed amm-v4 20285252 (100,034,383 lamports, 1 orphan share of 4,294), cpmm 20285226 (17,992,886, 1 of 3,055) and mixed 20295515 (11,721,742, 1 of 1,621) too, but there a lender kept the dust shares it could not withdraw and the orphan took only its 1/S of a vest (or of acc_r built while S was smaller still), large because S was a few thousand shares; see fuzz-m10-24h-a-cpmm-carry-owed.json for the carry-rounding shapes. Replay: `shortwin-fuzz replay tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz-m10-24h-a-curve-orphan-credit.json`.
